predecessors.name: Shaybanids
predecessors.text: the land between the Amu Darya and the Syr Darya that remained to the Uzbeks after Shaybani's death

successors.name: Emirate of Bukhara
successors.text: the whole khanate: 'In 1785, his descendant, Shah Murad, formalized the family's dynastic rule' as emirs

rulers.name: Muhammad Abd al-Mumin
rulers.title: puppet khan under the Manghit ataliq

rulers.name: Muhammad Ubaidullah II
rulers.title: puppet khan under the Manghit ataliq

ledger.x: 1512: Babur is beaten at Ghazdewan and the Uzbeks keep Transoxiana.
1512: Babur takes Samarkand.
1512: Ghazdewan ends the contest for Samarkand; the Uzbeks recover it.
1512: Bukhara recovers Balkh from Babur.
Winter 1516-17: the Uzbeks march on Tashkent.
About 1521: Kasym Khan's reign ends with the Syr Darya towns Kazakh.
About 1521: Tashkent, Turkestan and the Syr Darya steppe are Kazakh (see above); the year is Cliopatria's shape change and Kasym's reign end.
1528: Ubaydullah Khan 'recaptured Astarabad and Mashhad' and besieges Herat; Tahmasp relieves it and wins at Jam on 24 September 1528 ('Ultimately the Safavids emerged victorious').
Late 1530: the Safavids drive the Uzbeks out of Khorasan again.
1538: Ubaydullah Khan marches into Khwarazm, killing the local khan Avanish.
1538-39: Din Muhammad drives Ubaydullah out, and he dies in 1539 shortly after the Khwarazm defeat.
1576: Abdullah Khan II takes Tashkent.
ledger.cp: Shaybanid appanage of Samarkand and Tashkent

ledger.x: 1584: Abdullah Khan II seizes Badakhshan (He seized Badakhshan).
1588: Khorasan is seized in the war with Iran that began in 1587 (He started a war with Iran in 1587 that lasted until 1598).
1593: Abdullah Khan II conquers Merv.
1593-94: His troops conquered Khwarazm.
1598: Abdullah Khan II dies and the occupation of Khwarazm lapses.
1598: Tauekel's Kazakhs overrun the east.
1598: the war with Iran ends in a Safavid recovery of Khorasan.
1598: Balkh passes to the Safavids.
1599: the Janid (Ashtarkhanid) dynasty replaces the Shaybanids.
1600: Merv goes to the Safavids.
1601: Balkh returns to Bukhara (Safavid rule 1598-1601).
1609: Samarkand and Fergana are Bukharan again in Cliopatria's shape.
1646: Shah Jahan takes Balkh.
1647: the Mughals lose Balkh again and Bukhara holds it.
1709: the Fergana valley breaks away.
1734: Ura-Tyube becomes the front with Kokand.
1736: Nader Shah conquers Balkh.
1747: the ataliq Muhammad Rahim kills Abu al-Fayz and his son, 'ending the Janid dynasty'; Manghit ataliqs rule behind Janid puppet khans until 1785.
1748: the north-western desert (Kyzylkum, Zarafshon) is Khiva's in Cliopatria's Khiva row.
November 1762: 'Bukharan armies conquered the town of Charjuy and subdued the Turkmen.'
1785: the khanate ends; the fighting over Ura-Tyube goes on into the Emirate period (for 140 years from 1734 on the Kokand page).
1785: Shah Murad becomes emir.

wars.name: Battle of Ghazdewan and the Babur-Uzbek war
wars.outcome: Babur takes Samarkand briefly and is beaten at Ghazdewan in 1512; the Uzbeks keep the land between the Amu Darya and the Syr Darya.

wars.name: Uzbek-Kazakh war over Tashkent and Turkestan
wars.outcome: Kasym Khan holds the Syr Darya towns; the Uzbek advance on Tashkent in the winter of 1516-1517 fails.

wars.name: Battle of Jam and the Uzbek-Safavid war over Khorasan
wars.outcome: Ubaydullah recaptures Astarabad and Mashhad and besieges Herat; Tahmasp wins at Jam on 24 September 1528 with artillery; Herat is surrendered later and the Safavids expel the Uzbeks by late 1530.

wars.name: Ubaydullah Khan's Khwarazm campaign
wars.outcome: Ubaydullah kills Khan Avanish and is driven out by Din Muhammad; he dies in 1539.

wars.name: Abdullah Khan II's war with Safavid Iran
wars.outcome: Abdullah II seizes Khorasan (1588) and Merv (1593); the Safavids retake Balkh (1598-1601), Merv (1600) and Khorasan after his death.

wars.name: Abdullah Khan II's conquest of Khwarazm
wars.outcome: Khwarazm is occupied and the Khivan sultans executed; the Arabshahids return after 1598.

wars.name: Kazakh invasion of Transoxiana under Tauekel
wars.outcome: Tauekel takes Tashkent, Turkestan, Andijan and Samarkand in 1598 but fails to take Bukhara.

wars.name: Mughal occupation of Balkh
wars.outcome: Shah Jahan makes Balkh a Mughal subah in 1646 and loses it in 1647.

wars.name: Nader Shah's Central Asian campaign
wars.outcome: Nader conquers Khiva and forces Bukhara to submit in 1740; Abu al-Fayz 'remained on the throne' as a vassal ('conquered by Persia', Janid page).

wars.name: Bukhara-Kokand wars over Ura-Tyube
wars.outcome: Constant fighting: Urateppe 'would be the focal point of almost constant fighting' with Bukhara for 140 years; Kokand keeps most of Khujand.

certainty.note: Oasis frontiers between a khanate of appanages, Kazakh and Turkmen nomads and Persia: no treaty line is drawn in this period.
